newsitem.title: UK: Guinness, Grand Metropolitan announce merger.
newsitem.headline: Guinness, Grand Metropolitan announce merger.

text.p: Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc shook the stock market on Monday with surprise plans for a merger creating the world's seventh largest food and drink company, worth more than 23 billion pounds ($37 billion).

The merger will form the world's leading spirits and wine company, bringing together brands such as GrandMet's Smirnoff vodka, J&B whisky and Bailey's with Guinness-owned Johnnie Walker and Bell's Scotch whisky and Gordon's gin.
GrandMet's strong U.S. food interests through Burger King and Pillsbury will be united with Guinness' brewing operations based around its world-famous stout ale.

Guinness shareholders will retain their shares in the renamed GMG under the deal. GrandMet shareholders will receive one GMG share for every GrandMet share they hold, leaving GrandMet shareholders with 52.7 percent of GMG.
In addition, shareholders will get a cash payout of at least 60 pence a share, totalling 2.4 billion pounds.

It means the Guinness name will disappear as a corporate identity after 248 years. Formed in Dublin in 1759, the brewer changed its name from Arthur Guinness & Sons to Guinness Plc in 1985, the year before it launched a bid for spirits company Distillers Plc.

Shares in the two companies surged on the merger news as investors and analysts looked to cost savings from the deal, particularly in spirits, as well as the one-off cash handout. "It makes total sense, there is virtually nothing that does not fit," said Dermot Carr, analyst at Nikko Europe.
On Friday's share prices, the combined value of the group was 20.61 billion pounds, making it the seventh largest food and drinks company worldwide and Britain's eighth-largest quoted company.
But the value of the deal was boosted to more than 23 billion pounds as GrandMet shares rose 89 pence to 604 after touching 613 and Guinness shares jumped 97-1/2 pence to 614 after a high of 625.
Based on the value of the "junior partner" in the deal -- Guinness in this case -- the merger is the 10th largest in history.
The two companies' chairmen, George Bull of GrandMet and Tony Greener of Guinness, have been friends, and friendly rivals, for years and said the deal was hatched out over dinner last month.
"The discussions started because I invited Tony to dinner," Bull told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).

Greener then went to Africa for a week where he mulled the idea over. Upon his return, the two men sat down to just three weeks of discussions culminating in one of the largest mergers in British history.
Bull said he did not expect the merger to face regulatory problems as it would give the group less than 10 percent of accessible world spirits markets.
"We are entirely confident that we will be able to obtain the agreement of the regulatory authorities both here in Europe and also in the United States and elsewhere," he said.

The companies said they were convinced ther merger was in the best interests of all shareholders, although Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods and drinks group LVMH Moet Hennessy, which has a 14.2 percent stake in Guinness, voted against the deal as a non-executive director.

Arnault suggested an alternative which would involve a combination of the three spirits and wines businesses of GrandMet, Guinness and Moet Hennessy as an independent listed group. LVMH shares jumped some four percent to be quoted up 55 francs at 1433 on the merger news.

Bull will initially chair the new group jointly with Greener but will retire as planned in July 1998, leaving Greener as sole chairman. GrandMet's John McGrath will be chief executive, with the rest of the board made up of a balance of directors from both firms.
Bull said the move would, "create a combined spirits and wine company which will truly be a world leader so it will be able to grow faster at that stage than either would be able to do on its own."
GMG Brands' four divisions will be United Distillers and Vintners (UDV), the combined spirits and wines business, Pillsbury, Burger King and Guinness Brewing Worldwide.

The merger gives Guinness an increased interest in North America through GrandMet's Pillsbury and Burger King food divisions, while GrandMet shareholders will benefit from the Guinness spirits business in emerging markets.
Pilsbury brands include Green Giant vegetables and Haagen-Dazs icecream. Guinness stout is one of the world's most widely distributed beers, brewed in 50 countries and sold in about 150.

The companies estimate savings of about 175 million pounds a year in the third year of trading through integrating the sales force around the world, pruning back at head offices and savings in production.
Analyst Colin Davies of Goldman Sachs called this estimate "conservative", however, saying: "There is clearly a very good brand fit, a good geographic fit."

GMG chief executive-elect McGrath told a news conference there would be aorund 2,000 job losses out of 20,000 employed in the companies' spirits business. The two firms empoy a total of 85,000 worldwide.
GrandMet brought forward its first-half results to coincide with the merger news. Pre-tax profit rose by 3.5 percent to 471 million pounds before charges.
($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
